inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin may point to more tenancies, but that is no comfort to families facing eviction or homelessness. Rising notices and emergency accommodation show that stability—not a flattering headline—is what matters. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 may sound reassuring, but more regulation cannot substitute for a housing system that gives families secure homes and owners confidence to provide them. The government should be judged by whether people can remain housed, not by statistics that make insecurity look like progress.
inputs.modified_text: More tenancies mean little when families are still facing eviction and homelessness. The real failure is a housing system that leaves families without security while government reaches for more regulation and celebrates statistics. Six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 may sound reassuring, but owners need confidence to provide homes, not ever more interference. Stable homes matter for family life and social order; the government should be judged by whether people can stay housed, not by a flattering headline.
